# Validation of the expected-outcome models

**Synthetic data.** Every figure in this report is computed from a labelled
synthetic dataset generated by JudgeMetrics itself: no court, judge, or person
in it is real, and the figures describe the generator, not any justice system.

This report validates the expected-outcome models behind every
observed-to-expected ratio against the brief's model-validation tests: the
temporal train/test split, calibration curves, the Brier score, ROC AUC as a
secondary diagnostic, subgroup calibration, feature stability, missing-data
sensitivity, and the bootstrap stability of the judge-level estimates. It is
rendered by `judgemetrics validation report` and checked in CI with `--check`;
the methodology is docs/METHODOLOGY.md.

These statistics describe associations in available records. They do not prove
that a judicial decision caused a later event. An O/E ratio above 1 means
observed outcomes exceeded the model's expected count for the defined cohort. A
ratio below 1 means observed outcomes were below the model's expected count. It
must not be described as proof that the judge caused the difference.

## Dataset and versions

- Source `synthetic` (synthetic data): coverage 2016-01-01 to 2023-12-31;
  manifest seed 20260916, scale demo, generator version 3, truth version 3.
- Rows in the snapshot's frame of `synthetic`: cases 5200, charges 8335,
  assignments 6142, decisions 14168, sentences 3241, events 22229,
  justice_events 14894, persons 3200, courts 5.
- Outcome model specification version 3 (`expected-logit-v1`); metric registry
  version 3; methodology version 1.1.
- Thresholds: a model is fitted when its limiting class has at least 5 events
  per design column; a judge's ratio and a subgroup cell are published with at
  least 30 index events and 5 expected events; 500 person-cluster bootstrap
  replicates; 95% percentile intervals; the temporal split's test set is the
  index events at or after the 0.75 quantile of index time.

## Summary

Per target and window: the model's status, its index events (n) and outcomes
(O), and the temporal split's training and test rows and outcomes. The
diagnostics are measured on the test set, scored by a model refitted on the
training set alone (a calendar year unseen in training is scored at the last
training year's level): the Brier score and its skill against the training base
rate, ROC AUC, calibration in the large (observed over expected), and the
calibration slope (1 for a calibrated model).

## Temporal transport

Per calendar year of the index event: the index events, the observed rate, the
mean prediction of the published fit (which carries the calendar-year feature,
so within a year the two agree up to the penalty), and the side of the temporal
split the year falls on. The split's test years are unseen in training and are
scored at the last training year's level, so a trend in the observed rate across
years appears in the summary as calibration in the large away from 1, a slope
below 1, and a low test AUC, while the published fit absorbs the trend.

For the synthetic source, docs/SYNTHETIC_DATA.md "Temporal transport" explains
the trend the generator produces in the new-case rate.

## Feature stability

Per design column of the published fit (a feature at a level, against the
feature's reference; a court, jurisdiction, or year by its rank label or year,
never by an identifier): the estimate, the standard deviation over the converged
bootstrap replicates, and the share of replicates agreeing with the estimate in
sign. A share near 0.5 means the data cannot tell the column's direction.

## Missing-data sensitivity

Each model refitted without every index event that has a feature at its missing
level (complete cases), both fits scoring every row of the design so each
judge's cohort is unchanged; across the judges whose ratio is published, the
Spearman correlation of the two fits' pooled ratios and the largest absolute
change (max change). Excluded: eligible events dropped before the design under a
feature's exclude rule. Missing: design rows with a feature at its missing
level, which the complete-case refit drops.

## Bootstrap stability of the judge-level estimates

Over the judges whose ratio is published, as distributions (median and
quartiles), never per judge: the width of the 95% percentile interval of the
pooled ratio (median and interquartile range), the share of those intervals that
exclude 1, and the width of each judge's 95% rank interval (the judges ranked by
pooled ratio within every replicate). The interval is the bootstrap distribution
of the pooled estimate, which is shrunk toward 1: it describes that estimate's
sampling variability, not a confidence interval for the judge's true ratio.

## Subgroup calibration

Per model and restricted attribute value, aggregated over the index events: the
events, the observed outcomes (O), the expected count from the published model
(E), O/E, and its 95% percentile interval over the bootstrap replicates. The
model never reads a restricted attribute (the specification excludes them by
policy); this table shows what that choice leaves in the residual. A cell with
fewer than 30 index events or 5 expected events, or without a fitted model, is
withheld with its reason and shows no figure. The attributes are read from the
restricted schema by one module, as the ingest role, and never leave it below
the aggregate.

On the synthetic source the two attributes are controls. The filing-age band is
the positive control: the generator moves the failure-to-appear log-odds and the
next-filing exponent by band, and the model omits it, so its cells must show the
planted direction (younger bands above 1, older below). The synthetic group is
the negative control: drawn on its own stream and read by no draw, so every one
of its cells must be calibrated (O/E near 1).

## Recovery of the planted effects

On the database path - after ingest, entity resolution, the snapshot, and the
compute - the published pooled ratios of the judges with at least the
specification's minimum followed cohort, against the synthetic truth: the
Spearman correlation of the log pooled ratio with the court-centered planted
effect (raw: the raw rates' correlation, for contrast), the sign agreement over
the judges whose centered effect exceeds the threshold, the Pearson correlation
of the expected counts with the oracle's, and the share of published intervals
covering the true ratio, each against the specification's recovery block.

- `pretrial_release`: 20 judges; Spearman 0.934 (minimum 0.90; raw rates 0.689);
  sign agreed for 5 of the 5 judges whose centered effect exceeds 0.85;
  expected-count correlation 0.999 (minimum 0.95); interval coverage 0.600
  (minimum 0.55): met.
- `new_case`, 365 days: 19 judges; Spearman 0.719 (minimum 0.70; raw rates
  0.716); sign agreed for 13 of the 13 judges whose centered effect exceeds
  0.85; expected-count correlation 0.995 (minimum 0.95); interval coverage 0.632
  (minimum 0.55): met.
- `failure_to_appear`, 365 days: 19 judges; Spearman 0.963 (minimum 0.90; raw
  rates 0.871); sign agreed for 5 of the 5 judges whose centered effect exceeds
  0.85; expected-count correlation 0.986 (minimum 0.95); interval coverage 0.684
  (minimum 0.55): met.

## Limitations

The limitations of adjustment (unobserved confounding, model misspecification,
the restricted attributes excluded by policy, intervals conditional on the
specification) are stated under "Adjusted statistics" in docs/METHODOLOGY.md,
and the brief's statistical warnings under "Known limitations" there; they apply
to every figure in this report.
